purpose: Decision pack for the ownership-register sitting. Five seams, costed, with the no-decision default stated for each.

sources.jobber: data/jobber/jobs.json — client, address, coordinates, product, default assignee
sources.file: projects/briefs/technician-route-automation/territories.json (v9, read-only, to state what the file says)

method.hours: weeklyEq visits x that tech’s GPS cycle minutes per stop for that weekday / 60. cycle-times-gps byTechDow where a weekday sample exists, else byTech, else the global 19.5 min.
method.baseline: every one of the 1,063 assigned jobs costed on its as-built route-day. This is the board as it runs today.
method.optionCost: only the seam’s customers move; the rest of the board is held still. Hours after = baseline +/- the seam delta, so two seams cannot be added together without re-running both.
method.medoid: per tech-weekday, the real customer point minimising total distance to that route-day’s STABLE set (>= 3 stable, else all assigned). A centroid can land in water; a medoid is always a place the truck has been.
method.caution: Cycle time blends drive with on-site time, so dense ground flatters a tech and spread ground penalises one. Cory is flattered, Luke and Alias are penalised.

recommendation.option: A — ratify the field: Robert Norton
recommendation.line: Ratify Robert — but decide it in the same breath as S2, because the two are one swap. Alone, enforcing the file moves 87 customers onto Cory and throws the fleet spread to 28.5 h. Taken with S2, enforcing both is defensible on paper: spread 15.3 h against 17.5 h for ratifying and 18.1 h today, and it puts each man back on his own doorstep. It still loses, for two reasons the table does not show: it moves 170 customers against 17, and it hands a block with the cleanest rhythm on Robert’s board (Friday 53 / Wednesday 38) to the tech whose own book is 4% day-stable.

recommendation.option: A — ratify the field: Cory Ventura
recommendation.line: Ratify Cory, as the other half of that swap. 77 of 88 are already his, and enforcing this half alone puts Robert at 55.3 h — the heaviest week anyone has run. Be honest about the price of ratifying: Robert lives in Maple Valley, a median 7 km from this block against Cory’s 31.1 km, and Cory lives in Buckley, 8.8 km from S1 against Robert’s 21.8 km. Ratifying asks both men to drive past each other every morning, unpaid. That is the argument for revisiting the swap once Cory’s book has a day grid — not for making it now.

seams.name: The 51 islands — customers held by a tech their neighbours contradict
seams.question: Fifty-one customers sit inside ground that a different tech’s settled work surrounds. Are they exceptions worth keeping, or drift to be tidied?

fileSays.note: territories.json has no concept of an island. Every one of these would be reassigned by zip on the next assign-by-territory run, with no record that it was deliberate.
